messages.subject: INLA - fails to run -  inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(): The inla-program exited with an error.
parts:
Hi All,

I am hoping you can help me with my error. I am running a mixed conditional Poisson regression but am quite new to INLA so do not understand the output of the errors. I have attached the error outputs. For some data, this runs fine and for others, I get the attached errors and I do not understand why. Any help would be much appreciated.

The first attachment (error_INLA_01.txt) is when I ran the model with verbose=TRUE and the second (error_INLA_02.txt) is when I ran it with verbose=TRUE,debug=TRUE, safe=FALSE.

Inla formula:
formula.ndvi <- case ~  -1 +
  ndvi_norm + 
  ndvi_norm:log_sl + 
  ndvi_norm:cos_ta +
  f(strt_n, model="iid", hyper = list(theta = list(initial = log(1e-6),
                                                   fixed = TRUE))) +
  f(ID_ndvi, ndvi_norm, values = 1:length(unique(dat$ind_f)), model="iid",
    hyper = list(theta = list(initial = log(1), fixed = FALSE,
                              prior = "pc.prec",param = c(1, 0.05))))

I ran the model:
inla.ndvi <- inla(formula.ndvi, family = "Poisson", data = dat,
                     control.fixed = list(
                       mean = mean.beta,
                       prec = list(default = prec.beta)),
                     control.compute = list(
                       dic = TRUE,
                       return.marginals.predictor=TRUE),
                     verbose=TRUE,debug=TRUE,safe=FALSE,
                     num.threads='2:1')

I have had different errors that I think may be a separate issues e.g.:
errors:
*** max_correction = 25.01 >= 25.00, so 'vb.correction' is aborted
*** Please (re-)consider your model, priors, confounding, etc.
*** You can change the emergency value (current value=25.00) by
*** 'control.inla=list(control.vb=list(emergency=...))'

I appreciate any help and advice.

Thank you,

Leila

parts:
you have 3.2*10^6 data and this is also the size of the latent model
(matrix size). I guess this is the issue (you'll run out of RAM)

[1] "MPredictor 0"
[1] "NPredictor 3260324"
[1] "NData 3260324"
[1] "y...fake has length 3260



if you share data/code I can try to run it on our server to verify

Best
Havard
